maya: Heads-up — I ran a couple of toy replays vs synthetic runs to probe continuous-batching behavior; noticed weird tail latency spikes when kernel-selector chooses int8-v2 for long contexts.
jordan: ah ok, can you paste the summary numbers?
maya: quick paste:
```
# run summary
mode,samples,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,mean_batch_size,kv_hit_rate
replay,10k,18,142,360,12.4,0.67
synthetic,10k,16,78,120,10.1,0.02
```

maya: replay shows much higher p95/p99 and bigger mean batch size (weird since we cap at 16).

sam: mean_batch_size 12.4 with cap=16 is fine, but p99=360ms is alarming. Was max_delay configured?
maya: max_delay_ms=12 for those runs. Also noticed when int8-v2 kernel is chosen p99 jumps; with f16 kernel selection p99 ~130ms.

alex: could be KV cache behavior — replay has prefix overlap so cache hits increase batching pressure; that sometimes interacts badly with token-level scheduling.
jordan: good point. Are we using standard scheduling policy (earliest-deadline-first) or tenant-priority?
maya: EDF default. Tenants are mixed in replay (3 tenants). I instrumented per-tenant batch sizes and saw tenant A monopolizing micro-batches during cache-warm window.

sam: can you share the small perf profile? even flamegraph snippet is fine.
maya: pasted stack for the 99th percentile sample (trimmed):
```
flamegraph snippet (p99 sample):
- scheduler::dispatch_loop  22%
- kernels::int8_v2::attention  18%
- kv::get_prefetch 12%
- runtime::serialize_response 10%
- other 38%
```

alex: scheduler dispatch being high suggests many small batches being created and torn down. That plus int8 kernel overhead for padding could explain tail.
jordan: hypothesis: replay's long prefixes cause kv hits which increase effective sequence lengths and push some requests into larger kernel paths where int8-v2 is slower for odd seq lengths. Need apples-to-apples: same sequence-length distribution across synthetic and replay.
maya: agreed. Proposed experiment: 1) Replay but truncate prefixes to N tokens to match synthetic seq length CDF. 2) Run with kernel selector forced to f16 vs int8-v2. 3) Collect per-tenant p50/p95/p99 and batch-size distribution and scheduling latency (time in queue).
sam: add a variant with delaycap=6 and batchcap=8 to see if stricter caps reduce tail. Also add run where KV prefetch disabled.

alex: +1. Also we should capture per-kernel invocation time histogram, and export KV hit/miss per request id to correlate.
maya: I'll spin up runs this afternoon. My run command (prototype) — paste:
```
./run_bench --mode=replay --trace=2026-03-12.trace --truncate-prefix=128 \
  --kernel-forced=f16 --max-delay-ms=12 --batch-cap=16 --out=run1.json
./run_bench --mode=replay --trace=2026-03-12.trace --truncate-prefix=128 \
  --kernel-forced=int8-v2 --max-delay-ms=12 --batch-cap=16 --out=run2.json
./run_bench --mode=synthetic --dist=trace-matched --out=run-synth.json
```
jordan: please also run with --collect-profiles and attach the raw pprof. ci-bot: would be great if we could auto-post diffs.

ci-bot: @maya noted — I'll post perf diffs if output paths are under ci-artifacts/bench/YYYYMMDD/*.json :robot_face:
maya: noted, I'll push to ci-artifacts/bench/20260318/. Expect ~3 runs x 4 variants => 12 artifacts.
sam: one more suggestion: add a noise workload (tiny random jitter on arrival timestamps) to avoid pathological simultaneous arrivals from replay. Replay often emits perfectly synced arrivals which amplifies batching.
maya: good call. I'll add --jitter-ms=5 as a variant.
alex: once we have data, we should compute fairness metric: per-tenant normalized tail latency (tenant p99 / global p99) and also a batch-hoarding metric (time fraction batches include 1 tenant only).
jordan: for the regression hunt — check recent kernel changes on int8-v2 in the last 3 commits (commit ids: a1b2c3d, d4e5f6). Maybe a micro change to padding logic.
maya: I'll correlate commit window. If int8-v2 shows systematically worse p99 for matched-length runs and similar KV hits, we file perf-regression ticket.
sam: please include small screencap of trace timeline (arrival vs dispatch) — helps visualize microbursting.
maya: will do. Starting runs now, I’ll drop updates here as they finish. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jordan: thanks — appreciate the thorough plan. Ping if you need GPUs.
maya: thanks all.
